narrative:
The bank’s decision to deny your loan was based on a careful review of your financial profile, and while the model’s assessment was close—predicting a 49% chance of you being a higher credit risk—it ultimately crossed the threshold that led to this outcome. This isn’t a reflection of your personal character, but rather a snapshot of factors that, when combined, suggested a need for greater caution.

The most influential factors in this decision were your **length of time at your current residence**, the **size of the loan you requested**, and your **employment history**. Your relatively short time living at your current address—just one year, compared to an average of nearly three years for approved applicants—raised some questions about stability. While this alone wouldn’t have been decisive, it contributed to the overall picture. The loan amount you sought was also slightly lower than the average approved request, but the model weighed it alongside other factors to assess whether it fit comfortably within your financial situation.

The biggest red flag, however, was your **recent start in your job**, with less than a year of employment. This is a critical signal for lenders, as consistent income over time is one of the strongest indicators of reliability. Most approved applicants had been in their roles for at least a few years, which provides a clearer sense of long-term stability. While your job is skilled and you’re financially supporting two dependents, the short duration made it harder for the model to confidently predict your ability to manage repayments over the full term of the loan.

To improve your chances in the future, focus on building a stronger track record in your current job and residence. If possible, aim to stay in your role for at least a couple of years before reapplying, as this would significantly strengthen your profile. Additionally, consider reviewing your savings and how the loan amount aligns with your disposable income—even small steps toward increasing your financial cushion could make a difference. The model’s decision isn’t final; it’s a guide, and with time and preparation, you can present a much clearer picture of your reliability.

The dataset contains information on a series of debtors that took a loan from the bank.

The target variable is whether the applicant will be a bad credit risk.

Protected attributes sex, age and foreign_worker were not used to make the machine prediction.

2. TECHNICAL EXPLANATION: SHAP VALUES
A SHAP value tells you how much a feature influenced the prediction (larger absolute value means a stronger influence) and its direction: positive pushes toward bad credit risk, negative toward good credit risk. Below are the top 3 features by absolute SHAP value.

Write a detailed narrative explanation tailored to this non-technical reader that MUST explain:
